about: Row status vectors (evidencebook#461, acceptance 6): each case's expect is the status of one term row as of input.at, written by hand from the rule in rowstatus/rowstatus.go's package comment; Go, Rust and Python must give exactly expect for every case and refuse every invalid input.

cases.name: r6-not-due-at-due-date
cases.why: no statement, T is the due date itself: not_due (up to and including)

cases.name: r6-no-statement-after-due
cases.why: no statement, T one second after the due date

cases.name: r6-cannot-tell-is-none
cases.why: cannot_tell counts as no statement

cases.name: r6-record-after-T-not-held
cases.why: a statement whose time is after T does not exist yet

cases.name: r5-waiting
cases.why: one side met, inside the window

cases.name: r5-waiting-at-window-end
cases.why: T is the window end itself: still inside

cases.name: r5-uncontested
cases.why: one side met, one second after the window end

cases.name: r5-latest-cannot-tell-clears
cases.why: the side's latest in-time statement is cannot_tell, so it has none; the other side's met stands alone

cases.name: r5-late-statement-ignored
cases.why: a statement after the window does not count and is not a concession (it is not the other side's value)

cases.name: r4-agreed-so-far
cases.why: Appendix A, 1 Nov: both say row 1 met, inside the window

cases.name: r4-agreed
cases.why: Appendix A: row 1 agreed from 5 Nov

cases.name: r4-agreed-not-met
cases.why: short case 2: both say not met, after the window: agreed, value not_met

cases.name: r3-disagreement
cases.why: Appendix A, 10 Nov: buyer not met, seller met, both in time

cases.name: r3-failed-check-overrides-agreement
cases.why: short case 1: both say met, the recomputed check (legs match) fails

cases.name: r3-failed-check-one-statement
cases.why: a failed recomputed check with one statement is still in disagreement

cases.name: r4-passed-check
cases.why: a passing check changes nothing

cases.name: cn-before-window-end-is-a-change
cases.why: inside the window a new statement simply replaces the side's own

cases.name: cn-disagreement-after-window
cases.why: the in-time values differ after the window

cases.name: cn-concession-counts
cases.why: after the window the seller gives the buyer's in-time value: agreed

cases.name: cn-concession-from-none
cases.why: a side with no in-time statement concedes to the other's value

cases.name: cn-cannot-tell-is-not-a-concession
cases.why: a late cannot_tell concedes nothing

cases.name: cn-only-first-counts
cases.why: the buyer concedes first; the seller's later concession does not count

cases.name: cn-simultaneous-count-none
cases.why: both concede at the same record time: neither counts

cases.name: cn-no-concession-profile
cases.why: a profile with no concession (Mesh): the late statement does not count

cases.name: r2-in-dispute
cases.why: Appendix A, 12 Nov: the buyer's dispute

cases.name: r2-withdrawn
cases.why: the claimant withdraws: the rules below apply

cases.name: r2-withdrawal-before-dispute
cases.why: a withdrawal is final for its side whichever was sealed first

cases.name: r2-other-side-withdrawal-no-effect
cases.why: only the claimant can withdraw its dispute

cases.name: r2-nonfinal-ruling
cases.why: Appendix A, 13 Nov: a ruling not yet final leaves the row in dispute

cases.name: r2-late-dispute
cases.why: after the window, on an agreed row, by a claimant that had seen the statement in time: late, no effect

cases.name: r2-late-dispute-unseen
cases.why: the claimant had not named the statement before the window ended: not late

cases.name: r2-late-dispute-failed-check
cases.why: a row whose check fails can always be disputed

cases.name: r2-late-dispute-on-disagreement
cases.why: in-time statements that differ are neither agreed nor uncontested: not late

cases.name: r2-late-dispute-uncontested
cases.why: after the window, on an uncontested row: late

cases.name: r2-late-dispute-ignores-concession
cases.why: lateness reads the in-time statements alone: a later concession does not make a dispute late

cases.name: r2-conflicting-final-rulings
cases.why: two forks of the case book with different first final rulings: no ruling applies, in dispute

cases.name: r1-ruled-remedy-due
cases.why: Appendix A, 21 Nov: final ruling, remedy due by 27 Nov

cases.name: r1-ruled-remedy-made
cases.why: Appendix A, 25 Nov: the refund is made

cases.name: r1-ruled-not-honoured
cases.why: the remedy date passed without one

cases.name: r1-ruled-late-remedy
cases.why: a remedy after its date: the date passed without one

cases.name: r1-first-final-wins
cases.why: of the named adjudicator's rulings only the first marked final counts

cases.name: r1-ruled-without-dispute
cases.why: a final ruling decides the row whatever else holds

cases.name: d-not-due-until-named-record
cases.why: Appendix A, 4 Nov: the seller said met, but row 3 is not due until the receipt record has a time

cases.name: d-waiting-after-receipt
cases.why: Appendix A, 4 Nov: once the receipt has a time, row 3 waits for the buyer, window to 18 Nov

cases.name: d-sound-item-uncontested
cases.why: the item arrived sound and nobody wrote again: uncontested after 18 Nov

cases.name: d-row2-agreed-so-far
cases.why: Appendix A, 4 Nov: row 2 due 5 Nov (4 days after the payment record), agreed so far

cases.name: d-row2-agreed
cases.why: row 2 agreed once its window, 3 days after its due date, has ended

cases.name: d-unset-up-to-latest
cases.why: no receipt record yet, T is the latest date: not due

cases.name: d-not-reached
cases.why: no receipt record by its latest date: not reached

cases.name: d-named-after-latest
cases.why: a payment record whose time is after its latest date does not set the dates

cases.name: d-named-after-T
cases.why: the named record exists only from its time: as of an earlier T the date is unset

cases.name: l-untimed-statement
cases.why: a statement with no time counts, and the result is local

cases.name: l-untimed-after-late
cases.why: an untimed statement after one of the same side that is already late is late too

cases.name: l-untimed-dispute
cases.why: a dispute with no time is never late and makes the result local

cases.name: b-r3-at-due
cases.why: in disagreement at T = the due date

cases.name: b-r3-at-window-end
cases.why: in disagreement at T = the window end

cases.name: b-r4-at-due
cases.why: agreed so far at T = the due date

cases.name: b-r4-at-window-end
cases.why: still agreed so far at T = the window end (inside)

cases.name: b-r5-at-due
cases.why: waiting at T = the due date

cases.name: b-r1-at-due
cases.why: ruled at T = the due date

cases.name: b-r1-at-window-end
cases.why: ruled at T = the window end

cases.name: b-r2-at-due
cases.why: in dispute at T = the due date

cases.name: b-r2-at-window-end
cases.why: in dispute at T = the window end

cases.name: b-dispute-at-window-end-not-late
cases.why: a dispute dated exactly at the window end is not after it: not late

cases.name: b-dispute-one-second-after-late
cases.why: one second after the window end: late

cases.name: b-statement-at-window-end-in-time
cases.why: a statement dated exactly at the window end is in time, not a concession (shown with concessions off)

cases.name: b-statement-one-second-after-late
cases.why: one second after the window end the same statement is late, and with concessions off it does not count

cases.name: b-remedy-at-its-date
cases.why: a remedy dated exactly at the remedy's date is made

cases.name: b-remedy-due-at-its-date
cases.why: T = the remedy's date with no remedy: still due

cases.name: l-untimed-cannot-tell
cases.why: an untimed cannot_tell that clears the side's earlier value makes the result local

cases.name: l-untimed-withdrawal
cases.why: an untimed withdrawal that removes a dispute makes the result local

cases.name: l-untimed-after-future
cases.why: an untimed statement after one of the same side dated after T is not held as of T

cases.name: d-ruling-over-unset-date
cases.why: a final ruling decides the row even before the receipt record has a time

cases.name: d-not-reached-over-ruling
cases.why: not reached is checked first, before any ruling
